3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The mood in the situation room was gloomy.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: My cabinet members were gathered to discuss the shooting outside the Palace. Lileas presented the initial report.

6.speaker: Lileas Graf
6.text: “I agree. We are re-evaluating our security measures. However, the recession has affected my ministry negatively.”

7.speaker: Iosef Lancea
7.text: “Only if we stay vigilant as a country... We must think about the upcoming budget.”

8.speaker: Nia Morgna
8.text: “Freedom of expression is part of our constitution. We can't have anyone, let alone an MP, shot for voicing different opinions.”

10.speaker: Lileas Graf
10.text: “Bernard Circas was shot dead at 9:03 pm in front of the palace gates. He was an elected independent member of Assembly and as you know, a famous communist."

11.speaker: Player
11.text: “What were the motivations of such a horrid act?”

12.speaker: Lucian Galade
12.text: “We should refrain from making the issue a political one from the start. It will only add fuel to the fire.”

13.speaker: Lileas Graf
13.text: “Regardless, a full investigation into all involved parties is under way. We will find the subversives and punish them soon enough, Mr. President.”

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: The meeting concluded and the ministers left the room with concerned looks. It was hard to anticipate what would happen next.

15.speaker: Lileas Graf
15.text: “The guards at the scene were fifty meters away and immediately took action by responding and killing the assailant who was identified as a member of the nationalist organization, Young Sords.”

16.speaker: Player
16.text: “An MP shot near the Palace. That is absolutely unacceptable.”

17.speaker: Lileas Graf
17.text: “Our investigators are suspecting a political assassination since the Young Sords have been threatening the communists for some time.”

18.speaker: Lileas Graf
18.text: “He has always been an infamous figure. His poems had a large impact in the spread of communist ideas in Sordland. Many considered him a threat.”

19.speaker: Lucian Galade
19.text: “This may well create a dangerous atmosphere where the left versus right political violence of the 1920s could spark once again.”

20.speaker: Player
20.text: “I fully agree. We should protect freedom of speech.”

21.speaker: Player
21.text: “The Malenyevist ideology that the Red Youth promotes poses threats to our country too. We should be cautious.”

22.speaker: Player
22.text: “The nationalist Young Sords have overstepped, and they must face consequences for such an extreme action.”

23.speaker: Petr Vectern
23.text: “A return to those days would be devastating. The coups are the reason why our country stagnated for a decade.”

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: Nia Morgna, the Minister of Justice, sighed.

25.speaker: Nia Morgna
25.text: “Our laws do, and for good reason. Silencing voices only results in fear and stagnation inside society.”

26.speaker: Narrator
26.text: Several police cars rushed past the Maroon Palace and everyone went silent.

27.speaker: Iosef Lancea
27.text: “All due respect, ma'am, but we shouldn't be quick to jump to conclusions before a full investigation has been conducted.”

28.speaker: Lileas Graf
28.text: “Agreed. We are always watchful of internal threats, like the banned Communist Party members who support a similar agenda as the Red Youth.”

29.speaker: Iosef Lancea
29.text: “Don't be stupid, woman. These organizations speak against the state. The Labor Union of Sordland is also in the same boat. I wouldn't be surprised if United Contana had a hand in supporting all of them.”

30.speaker: Lileas Graf
30.text: “I hear your concerns, our police do their best to uphold the rights of our citizens. We will prevent such an act from happening again by making sure our security measures are re-evaluated.”

31.speaker: Player
31.text: “I agree. Internal stability must be maintained. Our security funding might need to be increased.”

32.speaker: Player
32.text: “We should not lose sight of our real political goals, like the constitutional reforms.”

33.speaker: Player
33.text: “It is too soon to jump to conclusions. Reckless acts will have dire consequences.”

34.speaker: Lucian Galade
34.text: “Agreed. We need to be patient until we have the full picture.”

35.speaker: Lucian Galade
35.text: “I am sure the Minister of Interior has already taken the necessary precautions.”

36.speaker: Lucian Galade
36.text: “Agreed, these matters shouldn't distract us from what the people want us to do.”

46.speaker: Player
46.text: “Any threat to our power must be dealt with as soon as possible.”

47.speaker: Lucian Galade
47.text: “Any direct attack against the government and our people is a serious concern but we don't know enough to act on yet.”

48.speaker: Lucian Galade
48.text: “It seems that the tensions between the communists and nationalists will escalate further.”

49.speaker: Nia Morgna
49.text: “It will be very difficult to pass any meaningful change if there is chaos in the country.”

50.speaker: Lileas Graf
50.text: “You can be assured that our police units and intelligence units are on increased threat condition. Nobody should be able to move a finger against government officials.”

51.speaker: Petr Vectern
51.text: “This will be it for today then. We will convene again soon. Thank you all, and keep us updated.”

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: Nia had always been one of the only members of the Justice Ministry truly deserving of the name. She had survived countless attacks on her character while fighting corruption within the ministry, and rising to power had only compounded her sense of moral duty.

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: Minister of Defense Iosef Lancea grunted in disapproval. He towered over the rest of us in full military uniform, his many war medals conspicuously on display.

54.speaker: Narrator
54.text: Minister of Defense Iosef Lancea grunted in disapproval. He towered over the rest of us in full military uniform, his many war medals conspicuously on display.

55.speaker: Lileas Graf
55.text: “Fortunately, no. You were simply in the wrong place at the wrong time. Our security forces have no reason to believe anybody has motivations to act against the President of Sordland for now.”

57.speaker: Nia Morgna
57.text: “The Red Youth has condemned the killing but didn't stop there. They promised revenge.”

58.speaker: Nia Morgna
58.text: “This will in turn spark further aggression from the Young Sords. The whole cycle started because Bernard Circas expressed his views. We can't simply look away.”

59.speaker: Nia Morgna
59.text: “This is not a simple overstep but an attack on our country. Murder for political opinions is a thing of the past. Our administration is building something new.”

60.speaker: Nia Morgna
60.text: “These groups wouldn't resort to unconventional means if they were represented in our Assembly. The high electoral threshold and bans are making these factions extreme.”

61.speaker: Nia Morgna
61.text: “Justice will be served and the rule of law will return to this country stronger than ever.”

63.speaker: Player
63.text: “It's early, but will we attend the funeral?”

64.speaker: Iosef Lancea
64.text: “How can that be achieved when it is Bernard Circas we are talking about? He is *the* communist of Sordland.”

65.speaker: Iosef Lancea
65.text: “There aren't many sides. The state versus its enemies.”

66.speaker: Nia Morgna
66.text: “We had that before and know very well how it was.”

67.speaker: Iosef Lancea
67.text: “Agreed, ma'am. Our Gendarmerie will also help boost security in the rural areas where possible. There might be more violence to come.”

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: Minister of Defense Iosef Lancea grunted in approval. He towered over the rest of us in full military uniform, his many war medals conspicuously on display.

69.speaker: Lileas Graf
69.text: “Agreed. We will reach out to the NFP and ask them to calm the situation with the Young Sords. The two groups have ties and Mr. Kibener sees reason, after all, which can't be said about the Young Sords at times.”

70.speaker: Player
70.text: “You are right. We need to defuse the situation.”

71.speaker: Lucian Galade
71.text: “Yes, but we need to calm the country. If we take sides we could escalate the situation further.”

72.speaker: Lucian Galade
72.text: “Our government is capable to maintain security. Our job will be to reduce tensions.”

73.speaker: Lucian Galade
73.text: “In my opinion we should. The nuance here is to detach the person from the violent act.”

74.speaker: Lucian Galade
74.text: “It is difficult, but an elected official has been shot. This is unacceptable for our new administration. We need to make sure we show our stance by condemning it at the funeral.”

75.speaker: Narrator
75.text: Lucian took some notes after checking the latest newspapers and reports.

76.speaker: Player
76.text: “We can't fix the recession if there isn't stability.”

77.speaker: Player
77.text: “We can't pass any constitutional reform in such an atmosphere.”

78.speaker: Player
78.text: “We will make it through this and deliver our promises.”

79.speaker: Petr Vectern
79.text: “You are right. We need to trust our ministers to stabilize the situation if it comes to it.”

80.speaker: Petr Vectern
80.text: “No use worrying about it now. Let's analyze the effects first. We will cross that bridge when we come to it.”

88.speaker: Player
88.text: “Whoever is against the state is an enemy.”

91.speaker: Petr Vectern
91.text: “I'll do my best to help coordinate the administrative tasks.”

93.speaker: Narrator
93.text: She spat the last word out with some distaste.

94.speaker: Lileas Graf
94.text: "The president and his family were unharmed, praise God."
